name: Far LMS
author: oriolmarches

sections.description:
Far LMS turns a WordPress site into an online academy. Create your courses, sell them with a one-time Stripe payment and give each student a private dashboard and a virtual classroom to follow the lessons.

What the free version includes

  • Course builder: courses, modules and lessons with video (YouTube, Vimeo, Wistia, Loom, Dailymotion, Streamable or your own video files), descriptions and downloadable materials.
  • Virtual classroom with a modern video player, previous/next navigation, downloadable materials and lesson progress.
  • Lesson search: students type a word and see which course and module each lesson is in (in the student dashboard and with the [acad_lesson_index] shortcode).
  • Live figures for your sales pages: [acad_figure key="lessons"] shows how many lessons, courses, modules, materials or students you have, and updates itself when you add content.
  • Resource library mode: show any course as a grid with a search box and filters (author, level, category, topic and type).
  • One-time purchase per course (or of all courses) through Stripe: a Payment Link of your own or a Stripe Checkout session created with the price you set.
  • Student registration, login and password recovery pages, and a private student dashboard with progress and quick access to each course.
  • Student area: the classroom and the dashboard can open full screen, without your theme’s header and footer (optional). Students don’t see the WordPress toolbar and are sent to their dashboard if they open /wp-admin. An optional link to your community (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord…) in the dashboard menu.
  • The payment step links to your privacy policy and, if you want, to your terms and conditions page.
  • Course materials stored in a protected folder and served only to students with access.
  • Student management, payment history and import of students from other membership plugins.
  • White-label design: your academy name, logo, colors and editable texts.
  • Emails sent with WordPress (wp_mail), so they work with any SMTP plugin, or through the plugin’s own SMTP settings (with presets for Brevo, Mailgun, Amazon SES and Postmark).
  • Optional signed webhook to send new students to the CRM or automation tool you already use.
  • Translation ready.

Paid plans

There is also a premium plugin, Far LMS Pro, sold separately. Basic adds recurring subscriptions (with plan changes and fair proration), discount codes, drip content, quizzes, assignments, certificates, lesson comments, progress reports, gift vouchers and short links with click counts. Pro adds a built-in CRM (campaigns, automations, landing pages and forms), on-site payment with a sales funnel and abandoned-payment reminders, retention tools (medals, course preview, and a cancellation flow that offers a pause or a cheaper plan before someone leaves), student documents, one-to-one classes and a REST API for your course content. Agency is Pro for up to 10 sites. You can try Pro for 7 days, with no card, on our website, where you get a trial key and the Pro plugin. Far LMS Pro replaces the free plugin and keeps all your data.

This plugin is complete on its own: it has no license checks, nothing in it is locked or stops working after a while, and the code of the paid features is not included in it.

Shortcodes

The plugin creates its pages on activation, so you do not need to add these by hand. They are listed here in case you want to build your own pages.

  • [acad_aula_virtual course="course-key"] – the virtual classroom of a course.
  • [acad_dashboard] – the student dashboard.
  • [acad_lifetime_plans] – the one-time purchase options.
  • [acad_checkout] – the payment step.
  • [acad_login], [acad_register], [acad_lost_password], [acad_reset_password] – account pages.
  • [acad_lesson_index] – lesson search for logged-in students.
  • [acad_figure key="lessons|courses|modules|materials|students"] – a live number for your sales pages.

External services

This plugin connects to the following third-party services. Nothing is sent until you configure the related feature.

Stripe

Used to take payments. When a visitor buys a course, the plugin sends the product name, price and the buyer’s email address to Stripe to create a Checkout session, or redirects to the Stripe Payment Link you entered (checkout.stripe.com / buy.stripe.com). Stripe sends payment notifications back to your site (webhook). For subscriptions that already exist on your Stripe account, the plugin sends the Stripe subscription ID when a student or you cancel it, and the Stripe customer ID when a student opens the Stripe customer portal (billing.stripe.com) from their dashboard. Requests go to api.stripe.com with your own Stripe keys.
Terms: https://stripe.com/legal/ssa — Privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy

Google reCAPTCHA (optional)

Only if you add reCAPTCHA keys in LMS → Settings. The registration page loads the reCAPTCHA script from www.google.com, and the plugin sends the visitor’s response token and IP address to Google to verify it.
Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Video platforms

Lessons can embed videos you host on YouTube (privacy-enhanced youtube-nocookie.com mode; the player loads YouTube’s IFrame API from www.youtube.com), Vimeo, Wistia, Loom, Dailymotion or Streamable. The player loads the video from that platform when a student opens the lesson. To show lesson thumbnails and the video poster, the classroom loads the image from img.youtube.com / i.ytimg.com or asks Vimeo’s oEmbed endpoint (vimeo.com/api/oembed.json) for it, and Vimeo videos use Vimeo’s player script (player.vimeo.com/api/player.js). All of this happens in the student’s browser when a lesson is opened. No personal data is sent by the plugin; the platforms receive the usual browser request.
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy — Vimeo: https://vimeo.com/terms and https://vimeo.com/privacy — Wistia: https://wistia.com/terms and https://wistia.com/privacy — Loom: https://www.atlassian.com/legal/cloud-terms-of-service and https://www.atlassian.com/legal/privacy-policy — Dailymotion: https://legal.dailymotion.com/en/terms-of-use/ and https://legal.dailymotion.com/en/privacy-policy/ — Streamable: https://terms.streamable.com/ and https://terms.streamable.com/privacy-policy

Your CRM webhook (optional)

Only if you enter a webhook URL in LMS → Settings. When a student signs up, cancels or is removed, the plugin sends the event name and time, your site address and the student’s email address, first name, last name and plan to that URL, signed with your secret. The “Send a test” button sends one test event with your own email address. You choose the destination service and its terms apply.

Email sending services (optional SMTP)

Only if you turn on the plugin’s own SMTP sending in LMS → Mail and choose one of these providers (otherwise WordPress sends the email as usual). Every email the site sends (to students and to you) then goes through that provider’s SMTP server with the account details you enter: the recipient’s address, the subject and the message. The “Send a test email” button sends one email to the address you type.
* Brevo (smtp-relay.brevo.com): Terms https://www.brevo.com/legal/termsofuse/ — Privacy https://www.brevo.com/legal/privacypolicy/
* Mailgun (smtp.mailgun.org): Terms https://www.mailgun.com/legal/terms/ — Privacy https://www.mailgun.com/legal/privacy-policy/
* Amazon SES, a service of Amazon Web Services (SMTP host email-smtp.REGION.amazonaws.com, for example email-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, in the region you choose): Terms https://aws.amazon.com/agreement/ and https://aws.amazon.com/service-terms/ — Privacy https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/
* Postmark (smtp.postmarkapp.com): Terms https://postmarkapp.com/terms-of-service — Privacy https://postmarkapp.com/privacy-policy
If you enter another SMTP server, that server receives the emails and its own terms apply.
When you save the email settings or press “Check now” in LMS → Mail, the plugin looks up the public DNS records (SPF, DKIM and DMARC) of your sender domain through your server’s normal DNS resolver. Only the domain name is used.

Gravatar (profile pictures)

The student dashboard shows the student’s profile picture. If the student has not uploaded their own photo and “Show Avatars” is on in Settings → Discussion, the plugin uses the WordPress avatar (get_avatar_url()), which by default is loaded from Gravatar (secure.gravatar.com), a service of Automattic. The student’s browser requests the image using a hash of their email address when the dashboard is shown. If “Show Avatars” is off, the plugin shows its own placeholder image and nothing is requested from Gravatar.
Terms: https://wordpress.com/tos/ — Privacy: https://automattic.com/privacy/

Far LMS website (links only)

The plugin’s “My plan” page has links to the pricing page (farlms.com) and to the Pro trial page (llicencies.farlms.com). Nothing is sent automatically: only if you click the trial link, your browser opens that page with your site address and language filled in. The plugin itself never connects to our servers.
Terms: https://farlms.com/terms/ — Privacy: https://farlms.com/privacy-policy/

Third-party libraries

The plugin bundles these open-source libraries in minified form. Their full source code is available at the links below.

  • Plyr 3.8.5 (video player), MIT license: https://github.com/sampotts/plyr
  • Sortable 1.15.7 (drag and drop in the course builder), MIT license: https://github.com/SortableJS/Sortable
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New, or upload the folder to wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. The plugin creates its database tables and the pages it needs (checkout, dashboard, one-time purchase, login, registration and password recovery).
  3. Go to LMS → Settings and add your Stripe keys (test keys work for trying it out) and your Stripe webhook secret. The webhook URL is shown on the same page.
  4. Create your first course in LMS → Course content and set its price in LMS → One-time sale.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Stripe account?

Yes, to take payments. Payments are processed by Stripe; the plugin never sees card details.

Where are my API keys stored?

In the WordPress options table (LMS → Settings), or as constants in wp-config.php if you prefer. They are never sent anywhere except to Stripe.

Can I sell subscriptions with the free version?

No. This plugin sells one-time purchases: one course, or all courses, for a single payment. Selling recurring subscriptions is a feature of the separate Far LMS Pro plugin. If you already have subscribers (for example, after moving from Far LMS Pro back to this plugin), this plugin keeps managing them: renewals, cancellations and the Stripe customer portal keep working.

How much does the premium version cost?

Per license, monthly or yearly (VAT not included): Basic €35/month or €290/year (1 site), Pro €69/month or €590/year (1 site) and Agency €139/month or €1,190/year (up to 10 sites, everything in Pro). Every paid plan has a 30-day money-back guarantee. This plugin costs nothing and has no time limit.

Is anything locked or time-limited?

No. Every feature of this plugin works without a license and without an expiry date, and the plugin contains no license checks. The optional 7-day trial is a trial of the separate Far LMS Pro plugin: it only starts if you request it yourself on our website.

Which video platforms can I use?

YouTube (in privacy-enhanced mode), Vimeo, Wistia, Loom, Dailymotion, Streamable and your own video files (MP4, WebM, MOV and others). Paste the video link in the lesson and the classroom does the rest.

Can I put my course pages at any address?

Yes. Add [acad_aula_virtual course="course-key"] to any page; the page does not need to have the same name as the course.

How do I show the number of lessons on my landing page?

Use [acad_figure key="lessons"] (or courses, modules, materials, students). Add floor="10" to round down to tens (127 becomes 120), round="50" to round to the nearest 50, and course="course-key" to count a single course.

Does it work with my theme?

The plugin pages use their own full-width template, tested with block themes and classic themes.

Can students keep access if I stop using a paid plan?

Yes. Courses, students and their access are stored on your site and are not removed.
sections.changelog:
2.3.2

  • A logged-in student only goes to the Stripe payment page from a link or button with a security check (nonce); other links show a “Continue to payment” button first.
  • The subscriptions table index works on every MySQL version, and the database version is only saved when the tables exist.
  • Profile pictures: Gravatar is used only when “Show Avatars” is on; otherwise a local placeholder. Gravatar is documented in “External services”.

2.3.1

  • WordPress.org review: the free plugin no longer contains any license or plan checks, and the code for selling subscriptions and discount codes is only in Far LMS Pro.
  • Scripts and styles are loaded with the WordPress enqueue functions, and only on the screens that need them.
  • Safer handling of form input and of payment notifications from Stripe.
  • Database tables are created and upgraded with dbDelta correctly.
  • Updated bundled libraries: Plyr 3.8.5 and Sortable 1.15.7, with links to their source code in the readme.
  • Documented the optional SMTP email providers in “External services”.

2.3.0

  • New name: Far LMS (slug and text domain far-lms).
  • English is now the source language.
  • Lesson search for students, in the dashboard and as a shortcode.
  • Student area: optional full-screen classroom and dashboard, no WordPress toolbar or /wp-admin for students, community link, and a focus outline only when using the keyboard.
  • Student dashboard menu grouped into “Learn” and “My account”; the other courses open from a button in the classroom.
  • [acad_figure] shortcode: live numbers of lessons, courses, modules, materials and students for your sales pages.
  • Resource library mode for any course, with search and filters.
  • The payment step links to your privacy policy and optional terms page.
  • Course pages can have any address: the classroom reads the course from the shortcode.
  • YouTube video titles are no longer requested from a third-party service.
  • Email settings: your own sending service (SMTP presets for Brevo, Mailgun, Amazon SES and Postmark), test email, SPF/DKIM/DMARC check and WP-Cron health.
  • Course materials and student files stored in a protected folder.
  • Video player assets bundled with the plugin (no external CDN).
